sources.label: The discovery
sources.claim: Links the independent ESPARGOS, eSpDR and C5VRX discoveries.
sources.limit: Published October 1, 2026. A project summary, not a measurement of our hardware.

sources.label: ESPARGOS · ESP-SDR
sources.claim: Original ESP32 is supported. Current firmware provides raw I/Q bursts and snapshot FFTs on this chip.
sources.limit: Minimum 2 MB flash. Support does not prove reception on this particular board.

sources.label: Receive controls
sources.claim: ESP32 filter mapping is approximately 12–67 MHz. Extended tuning commands are attempts, not validated coverage.
sources.limit: Gain is uncalibrated; PLL lock and RF accuracy are not guaranteed outside the normal band.

sources.label: Original ESP32 capture path
sources.claim: Reserves 64 KiB; at most 16,380 pairs per snapshot; nominal 16/40/80 MS/s with 8/10-bit packed output.
sources.limit: Small sample windows and UART transfers produce gaps. Nominal sample rates are not clock calibration.

sources.label: Spectrum protocol & validation
sources.claim: Original ESP32 uses snapshot FFTs. Selected newer chips can keep RF capture running while processing selected windows.
sources.limit: Continuous spectrum updates are not the same as exporting every I/Q sample.

sources.label: ESPARGOS discovery notes
sources.claim: Uses the internal modem ADC path. Reports experimental coverage around 2.2–2.7 GHz and coherent multi-receiver arrays.
sources.limit: Do not transfer array capabilities to one dev board or treat historical S31 transport plans as current firmware features.

sources.label: eSpDR · continuous FPGA transport
sources.claim: ESP32-S3, two GPIO lanes, Artix-7 FPGA, DDR buffer and FT600 USB 3 support an 80 MS/s path.
sources.limit: Uses S3 dedicated GPIO and SIMD. The original LX6 board cannot use this firmware unchanged. Current clocking forwards an ESP-generated clock to the FPGA.

sources.label: C5VRX · 5.8 GHz video
sources.claim: ESP32-C5 receives analog FPV and demodulates in the hardware pipeline, with composite video via resistor DAC.
sources.limit: Requires C5 radio and peripherals. Bench results do not establish range performance; not supported on our ESP32.

sources.label: Espressif ESP32 datasheet
sources.claim: Dual LX6 up to 240 MHz, 520 KB SRAM, a 2.4 GHz radio and SPI/I2S/GPIO interfaces.
sources.limit: Chip capability is not an inventory of board wiring, antenna connector or fitted external RAM.

sources.label: RTL-SDR Blog V4 design
sources.claim: R828D with built-in HF upconverter, 500 kHz lower coverage, upper range around 1.766 GHz, filtering, SMA and 1 ppm TCXO.
sources.limit: Coverage and oscillator specifications are manufacturer claims; our probe establishes identity, not sensitivity or tuning accuracy.

sources.label: RTL-SDR sampling & applications
sources.claim: 8-bit I/Q, continuous USB streaming; 2.4 MS/s is a useful starting rate. Supports many narrowband demodulators.
sources.limit: High sample rates can lose samples; measure sustained delivery on this host. Both stock receiver configurations are receive-only.

sources.label: AtomVM programming guide
sources.claim: Native extensions and ports provide integration boundaries for low-level work.
sources.limit: No ready-made ESP-SDR binding has been verified here. Do not run high-rate I/Q handling in ordinary Erlang processes.

sources.label: OpenSpec workflow
sources.claim: Proposal, delta specs, design and tasks describe planned changes; archiving records accepted capabilities.
sources.limit: Installed CLI is 1.11.0. This site adds evidence-aware tracking copied from the local T-Display-K230 project.

sources.label: Adiuvo Forgix official design
sources.claim: RP2354, Trion T8F49 with 7,384 logic elements, PSRAM, USB 1.1 and 3.3 V I/O.
sources.limit: User-reported ownership; actual board revision, wiring and firmware are not inspected.

sources.label: Forgix LiteX / SPIBone demonstration
sources.claim: A demonstrated MicroPython and CPU-less LiteX route uses passive configuration pins for a bounded SPI transport.
sources.limit: A development example, not proof of our board or a high-rate SDR transport.
